name: Griot
description: Marinated pork chunks that are boiled until tender, then fried to achieve a perfectly crispy exterior while maintaining juicy, flavorful meat inside.
cultural: Griot is one of Haiti's most beloved dishes, often served at celebrations and family gatherings. It represents the fusion of African and French cooking techniques.

name: Soup Joumou
description: A hearty pumpkin soup traditionally served on January 1st to commemorate Haitian Independence Day. This soup symbolizes freedom and resilience.
cultural: This soup was once forbidden to enslaved people and is now eaten every New Year's Day as a symbol of independence and freedom.

name: Diri ak Djon Djon
description: Black mushroom rice with a distinctive earthy flavor and dark color from indigenous Haitian mushrooms. A true delicacy of Haitian cuisine.
cultural: Djon djon mushrooms are unique to Haiti and give this rice its signature black color and umami-rich flavor. Often served at weddings and special occasions.

name: Tasso
description: Spicy fried turkey or goat meat, marinated in citrus and Haitian spices, then deep-fried until crispy. A popular street food snack.
cultural: Tasso is a beloved street food often enjoyed with pikliz and fried plantains. It's especially popular during Carnival season.

name: Pikliz
description: Spicy pickled vegetable relish made with cabbage, carrots, peppers, and scotch bonnet. The essential condiment for nearly every Haitian meal.
cultural: No Haitian table is complete without pikliz. This fiery condiment adds heat and tang to griot, tasso, and rice dishes.

name: Lambi
description: Conch cooked in a rich Creole sauce with tomatoes, peppers, and aromatic spices. A luxurious dish for special occasions.
cultural: Lambi is considered a delicacy in Haiti and is often served at weddings, holidays, and important celebrations.

name: Accra
description: Crispy saltfish fritters made with salted cod, flour, and aromatic herbs. A popular appetizer and street food snack.
cultural: Accra is a favorite street food and party appetizer throughout Haiti.

name: Diri Kole ak Pwa
description: Rice and beans cooked together with coconut milk and spices. The quintessential Haitian staple served daily in most homes.
cultural: This dish is the backbone of Haitian cuisine, eaten almost daily and representing home cooking at its finest.

name: Legim
description: A hearty vegetable stew with eggplant, cabbage, carrots, and spinach, often cooked with beef or crab.
cultural: Legim represents Haiti's agricultural abundance and is a staple in many households.

name: Poulet aux Noix
description: Chicken in rich cashew sauce, a festive dish for celebrations.
cultural: Reflects French influence in Haitian cuisine.

name: Mayi Moulin
description: Creamy cornmeal with beans, a hearty breakfast staple.
cultural: A comfort food showcasing Haiti's corn heritage.

name: Bannann Peze
description: Twice-fried flattened plantains, crispy and soft.

name: Paté Kòde
description: Savory fried pastries filled with meat or vegetables.
cultural: Breakfast tradition sold by street vendors.

name: Bouyon
description: Hearty beef soup with root vegetables and dumplings.
cultural: Saturday soup day tradition in Haiti.

name: Pen Patat
description: Sweet potato bread pudding with coconut and spices.

name: Doukounou
description: Sweet cornmeal cake steamed in banana leaves.
cultural: Unique texture from banana leaf wrapping.
